items.title: The name
items.text: hollywoodvideo.com is live. In October 2026 it described itself as “The NEW Hollywood Video”, an entertainment news site with a blog, and carried a “©2026 Hollywood Video” notice.[^22] The page does not say who operates it, and we could not establish who owns the trademark.

items.title: The brands and domains
items.text: In October 2010 Movie Gallery’s estate submitted a plan to auction its intellectual property through StreamBank, including the Reel.com domain and trademark.[^21] Who bought the Hollywood Video name, and for how much, is **not in our sources**.

items.title: The stores
items.text: A bankruptcy judge approved the closing of Movie Gallery’s remaining stores on May 19, 2010, and going-out-of-business sales followed.[^20] The Associated Press put the number at more than 1,900.[^19] The date the last Hollywood Video closed is not in our sources.

items.title: Movie Gallery
items.text: The buyer went through Chapter 11 twice. Its shareholders received nothing in the first reorganization, and the company did not try to reorganize in the second.[^13][^18]

items.title: Game Crazy
items.text: The game departments went with the stores. Movie Gallery still counted 250 Game Crazy locations after the February 2010 closures; all were covered by the liquidation.[^17][^19]

items.title: Reel.com
items.text: After June 2000 Hollywood kept Reel.com as a content-only site funded by advertising.[^3] Ten years later it was one of the assets listed for auction, described by the seller as a possible competitor to movie review sites.[^21]

items.title: The rival
items.text: Blockbuster, whose bid Hollywood’s board turned away in 2005, filed for Chapter 11 on September 23, 2010, four months after Movie Gallery’s liquidation was approved.[^20][^24]

blocks.title: Who owned the name
blocks.subtitle: One founder, one buyer, two bankruptcies and an auction whose result we could not trace.

nodes.what: Founded in Oregon by Mark J. Wattles. First store opens in October.[^1]
Initial public offering. 25 stores at year end.[^1]
First bankruptcy. The trademark has been written down to $15.0M.[^13][^14]
Emerges with its old shares canceled. By late 2008 affiliates of Sopris Capital control 86.3% of the votes.[^13]
Second bankruptcy, then liquidation of all stores.[^15][^19]
Intellectual property sent to auction through StreamBank. The buyer is not in our sources.[^21]
An entertainment blog uses the name. Its owner is not identified on the site.[^22]

blocks.source: Hollywood Entertainment and Movie Gallery filings[^1][^10][^13][^14], Bloomberg News[^15], the Associated Press[^19], Domain Name Wire[^21] and hollywoodvideo.com.[^22]
